title: Delegate terms renew automatically, so continuation is the default and non-renewal is the Foundation's no-cause exit route
content:
A.6.1.1.2.3.1.4.4.3 appoints Delegates to "fixed six (6) month terms aligned to calendar half-years (January 1 – June 30; July 1 – December 31)" and specifies that "terms **renew automatically unless determined otherwise** by the Grove Foundation."

Automatic renewal makes inaction equivalent to reappointment. Nobody has to affirm a delegate's continuation, so an established delegate stays in place indefinitely without recurring approval, and the administrative cost of maintaining a roster stays near zero.

What the term structure adds is a third departure route alongside the two in the offboarding section. Automatic non-performance removal requires crossing a measured threshold; emergency removal requires enumerated cause. **Non-renewal requires neither.** It happens at a scheduled boundary, needs no allegation, and — read with A.6.1.1.2.3.1.4.8.2, where non-renewal is listed alongside onboarding and discretionary offboarding as a registry trigger — is a recognised administrative event rather than an exceptional one.

That matters because the other two routes both make a claim about the delegate. Removing someone for negligence or for missing votes is a public statement, potentially a contested one. Declining to renew says nothing, which lets the Foundation end a relationship for reasons that are real but not chargeable: an unproductive delegate who technically clears 85%, an over-concentrated roster, or a judgement about fit.

The alignment to calendar half-years is what makes it usable at scale — every delegate's term ends on one of two dates a year, so roster composition can be reviewed as a whole rather than delegate by delegate on rolling anniversaries. The cost is a governance discontinuity twice a year, and a corresponding concentration of the Foundation's discretionary power at those two moments.
description: Fixed six-month terms aligned to calendar half-years renew unless the Grove Foundation determines otherwise, giving it a scheduled way to end a delegacy without alleging non-performance or cause.
